claude-code.summary: Claude Code supports Agent Skills, subagents, and MCP; agent-surface generates canonical auto-invocable skills plus explicit-only high-impact workflows, subagents, first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire), and external skills.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged and may be selected automatically. Available high-impact commands use the same native surface with disable-model-invocation: true.

subagents.notes: Normalized subagents map access levels to Claude Code tool lists and native permission modes; writable shell workers use bypassPermissions while read-only roles keep read-only tools.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are generated/merged; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

external.notes: Registry-backed external Agent Skills are copied only from configured skill_roots that contain SKILL.md.

codex.summary: Codex CLI and IDE extension, which Codex documents as sharing one configuration (the ChatGPT desktop app is documented to share their MCP configuration; neither the extension nor the app is runtime-tested here): agent-surface generates canonical auto-invocable skills, explicit-only manual skills, custom agents, global AGENTS.md instructions, first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire) and external skills in the default ~/.codex and ~/.agents; project paths only via --dest; CODEX_HOME is not followed. Codex cloud is not targeted.

skills.notes: Canonical and manual workflows use the shared Agent Skills root. Canonical skills set allow_implicit_invocation: true; available high-impact workflows set it to false and require explicit $<name> invocation. Project paths only via --dest.

subagents.notes: Custom agents render as standalone TOML with name, description, developer_instructions, and sandbox_mode. Writable shell workers use danger-full-access; read-only roles remain read-only. Project paths only via --dest.

rules.notes: Always-on rules bundle into ~/.codex/AGENTS.md. A --dest project install also writes .codex/AGENTS.md there, which Codex does not discover.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are merged into mcp_servers; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in. Project paths only via --dest; Codex reads project config only in trusted projects.

external.notes: Registry-backed external Agent Skills are copied only from configured skill_roots that contain SKILL.md. Project paths only via --dest.

deepagents.summary: Deep Agents Code supports skills, instruction files, custom subagents, and MCP config; agent-surface generates skills, instructions, the representable worker subagent, and optional registry-backed MCP config.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged. Available high-impact commands are emitted as explicit-invocation compatibility skills with disable-model-invocation: true; host enforcement remains unproven.

rules.notes: Rules render as Deep Agents Code instruction files; project root AGENTS.md remains available for project-owned instructions.

subagents.notes: Deep Agents Code subagent files cannot configure per-subagent tools, so only the read-write-shell worker profile is emitted.

mcp.notes: Optional MCP output is registry-backed and generated by default; a category-filtered install adds or prunes it by category.

external.notes: Registry-backed external Agent Skills are copied only from configured skill_roots that contain SKILL.md.

goose.summary: Goose supports reusable recipe YAML files and Agent Skills; agent-surface renders canonical skills plus available manual commands as project recipes or user compatibility skills.

recipes.notes: Available high-impact commands render as project-oriented recipes; user-scope distribution uses explicit-invocation compatibility skills instead of writing recipes into HOME.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are non-destructively merged into Goose YAML `extensions` (type: stdio); user-scope only (config.yaml is user-global). The file is ~/.config/goose/config.yaml on macOS and Linux (XDG_CONFIG_HOME is not followed) and Block\goose\config\config.yaml in the roaming AppData directory on Windows (%APPDATA% by default), resolved from the profile home, so a redirected %APPDATA% is not followed; the Windows route is not natively qualified. Windows installs made before the per-OS route merged into ~/.config/goose/config.yaml, which Windows Goose never reads; the next full install prunes those entries.

skills.notes: Canonical skills use Goose native Agent Skills discovery. User-scope high-impact commands share this root with disable-model-invocation: true; host enforcement remains unproven.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

grok-build.summary: Grok Build supports Agent Skills, project AGENTS.md instructions, custom agents, TOML configuration, and MCP; agent-surface generates skills, instructions, native agents, first-party MCP wiring, and always-approve execution policy.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged. Available high-impact commands are emitted as explicit-invocation compatibility skills with disable-model-invocation: true; host enforcement remains unproven.

rules.notes: Project instructions use the AGENTS.md compatibility family; scoped policies remain separate references.

subagents.notes: Normalized access maps to a typed capabilityMode (read-only, read-write or all) narrowed by a tools allowlist, with mcpInheritance none. No model is written, so the child inherits the parent's model, and no permissionMode, since Grok wires only bypassPermissions. Grok always also loads .claude/agents: within one directory the native file wins, but a project or deeper .claude/agents copy shadows a user-scope native agent. grok 1.0.40 lists all six from .grok/agents in a clean project and beside .claude/agents copies (grok inspect --json, 2026-09-30); tool enforcement on a spawned child is not yet observed.

external.notes: External skill packs mirror into the same skill root as canonical skills.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are merged into mcp_servers; the ui.permission_mode setting is always-approve. External or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

dsh.summary: DSH Developer Preview natively discovers Agent Skills; agent-surface limits this adapter to canonical and reviewed external skills while its profile and MCP contracts remain unstable.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for automatic and explicit native skill discovery. Manual command artifacts are intentionally not generated.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skills use the same discovery roots.

notices.message: CVE-2026-82533 (critical) affects DeepSeek Harness builds before 0.1.2-alpha.1. This notice does not check the installed build.
notices.action: Read the installed package version without launching the client and upgrade an affected build before using it. This adapter is not requalified on fixed builds.

pi.summary: Pi coding agent CLI (npm @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent; the @mariozechner package is deprecated): agent-surface generates skills, explicit-only compatibility skills, AGENTS.md instructions and external skill packs in the default ~/.pi/agent (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is not followed) or project roots.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged. Available high-impact commands are emitted as explicit-invocation compatibility skills with disable-model-invocation: true, which Pi documents as hiding the skill from automatic selection; not runtime-tested. Project .pi/skills need project trust.

rules.notes: Rules are bundled into Pi instruction files.

external.notes: External Agent Skills mirror into Pi skill roots.

mcp.notes: No stdio MCP configuration format verified for Pi; first-party MCP is not generated.

pool.summary: Poolside CLI: agent-surface generates local skills, AGENTS.md instructions (personal ones at Poolside's default ~/.config/poolside/AGENTS.md; Poolside honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME, which agent-surface does not follow) and external skill packs, and merges MCP config (mcp_servers) non-destructively into settings.yaml.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged. Available high-impact commands are emitted as explicit-invocation compatibility skills with disable-model-invocation: true; host enforcement remains unproven.

rules.notes: User installs write the documented personal ~/.config/poolside/AGENTS.md; project installs use AGENTS.md. Earlier installs wrote ~/.config/poolside/.poolside. When a selection writes the personal instructions, an owned copy identical to the replacement is removed after the write, and a differing one blocks with MIGRATION_SOURCE_CONFLICT because no recorded qualification shows the client ignores it; other selections leave it in place and claimed. Native discovery of either route is not yet qualified.

external.notes: External Agent Skills mirror into Poolside local skill roots.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are non-destructively merged into Poolside YAML `mcp_servers`; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

cline.summary: Cline supports workflows, rules, Agent Skills, Configured Agents, MCP, plugins, hooks, scheduling, connectors, built-in spawn_agent delegation, and agent teams. The agent-surface subagents primitive compiles to Cline Configured Agent YAML; spawn_agent is separate runtime behavior that needs no generated artifact. agent-surface also generates workflows, rules, external skills, the ignore file, and first-party MCP wiring for the CLI plus installed VS Code/Cursor/Windsurf extension routes.

commands-as-workflows.notes: Available high-impact commands render as manual workflows; safe reusable procedures are native skills.

rules.notes: Always-on rules are bundled into one file under the shared CLI/extension global rules directory. Scoped rules remain reference-only because Cline's rules loader does not recursively discover the references directory.

subagents.notes: The agent-surface subagents/*.md source primitive compiles to Cline Configured Agents. Cline only discovers .yaml/.yml definitions; generated tool allowlists preserve normalized read-only, read-write, and shell access. These definitions are distinct from the built-in spawn_agent runtime tool.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for model selection through Cline use_skill. Available high-impact commands remain native workflows.

mcp.notes: Only the CLI and Cline's SDK-based extension (the Next bundle, rolling out from 4.1.0) read the shared ~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json; the pre-SDK extension that 3.x and most 4.x installs run reads settings/cline_mcp_settings.json under its IDE's globalStorage. First-party secretless MCP services are merged into the shared route and into each per-IDE route whose IDE has the Cline extension installed (an extension folder, or a symlink to one, that the IDE has not marked obsolete); extension storage is not a signal because IDEs keep it after an uninstall, and a custom extensions directory is not detected. A full install prunes servers agent-surface merged into a per-IDE route whose IDE has no Cline, and plans list skipped routes with the reason. No Devin Desktop route is written. Scope-derived Windows installs honor APPDATA, and explicit --dest installs relocate the conventional AppData/Roaming subtree. External or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in. Documentation mentioning .cline/mcp.json is not backed by the current loaders.

plugins.notes: Cline plugins are executable code. agent-surface has no Cline plugin source primitive and does not generate or install them.

hooks.notes: Hooks are executable files. agent-surface has no hook primitive and does not infer executable hooks from rules, commands, or subagents.

scheduling.notes: Cline cron specs and schedule state are automation surfaces with independent execution semantics. agent-surface does not convert command workflows into unattended schedules.

connectors.notes: Connector settings can contain credentials and external delivery configuration, so they remain user-owned.

provider-settings.notes: Provider and model selection can contain credentials and host-specific choices; agent-surface does not own this configuration.

runtime-subagents.notes: Cline's built-in spawn_agent tool creates focused subagents at runtime. It consumes no agent definition file and is separate from Configured Agents generated by the subagents render token.

agent-teams.notes: Persistent team state is created and managed by the Cline runtime; agent-surface does not generate or modify it.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

kilo.summary: Kilo supports workflows, instructions, subagents, skills, MCP, and ignore files; agent-surface generates workflows, AGENTS/rule files, subagents, ignore files, and a safe kilo.jsonc merge with full-access execution and automatic sharing disabled.

commands-as-workflows.notes: Available high-impact commands render as manual custom commands; safe reusable procedures are native skills. Automatic session sharing remains disabled.

rules.notes: Always-on rules are emitted as files and registered through the instructions array; scoped language rules are emitted as references.

subagents.notes: Subagents render as Kilo mode: subagent markdown. Read-only roles deny all capabilities by default and allow only read/search/skill tools; writable shell workers allow the full tool surface.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are merged into the existing mcp map; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in. Full installs apply the declared full-access/share-disabled host policy, while category-only MCP installs preserve existing host-wide policy.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for Kilo use_skill discovery. Available high-impact commands remain native custom commands.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

kimi-code.summary: Kimi Code CLI (TUI, print and web) and the Kimi Code for VS Code extension (in VS Code and Cursor), sharing KIMI_CODE_HOME: agent-surface generates skills, instructions, custom agents and MCP, and configures terminal Auto and editor kimi.yoloMode. Kimi Code Desktop is not targeted.

evidence.label: Kimi Code VS Code extension shared configuration

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged and model-invocable. Available high-impact commands render as explicit-only type: flow skills with disableModelInvocation: true.

rules.notes: Always-on rules render into Kimi's instruction file; scoped language rules remain reference files until a matching workflow attaches them.

subagents.notes: Custom agent Markdown maps normalized access to Kimi tool allowlists. The generated profiles are available to native delegation; --agent can also select one as the main agent in print mode or the TUI, which agent-surface does not configure.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are merged as native command-plus-args stdio entries. External or secret-bearing services remain opt-in.

settings.notes: Full installs set terminal default_permission_mode to auto and editor kimi.yoloMode to true without replacing sibling settings. The extension exposes YOLO, not persistent Auto; category-only MCP installs preserve host-wide policy. Project .kimi-code/config.toml is not a documented Kimi config file (the project file is .kimi-code/local.toml), so project Auto and merge_all_available_skills are not claimed.

runtime-subagents.notes: Kimi's built-in coder, explore, and plan sub-agents are runtime behavior; generated custom profiles supplement them.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native Kimi skill roots.

plugins.notes: Kimi plugins can package skills, commands, agents, hooks, and MCP, but agent-surface emits the corresponding native file surfaces directly.

hooks.notes: Executable hooks have no matching agent-surface source primitive and are not synthesized.

provider-settings.notes: Provider, model, credential, and login state remain user-owned. The installer merges only the declared permission property.

qoder.summary: Qoder CLI natively supports Agent Skills, Markdown commands, AGENTS.md, custom subagents, JSON settings, MCP, and headless execution; agent-surface generates each stable file surface with bypass-permissions as the default mode.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged and remain available for automatic or explicit invocation.

commands.notes: High-impact workflows remain explicit slash commands in Qoder's Markdown command format.

rules.notes: Always-on rules use Qoder's user and project instruction files; scoped rules remain references.

subagents.notes: Normalized access maps to native tool allowlists and permissionMode values.

mcp.notes: First-party MCP entries, bypass permission mode, and the native-catalog-only skill source policy are deep-merged without replacing sibling settings.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skills use the same native roots.

qwen-code.summary: Qwen Code natively supports Agent Skills, Markdown commands, QWEN.md, custom subagents, JSON settings, MCP, and headless execution; agent-surface generates these surfaces with yolo approval mode.

skills.notes: Canonical skills remain model-invocable and directly slash-invocable.

commands.notes: High-impact workflows use the current Markdown command format, not deprecated TOML commands.

rules.notes: Always-on rules use Qwen Code's native context files; scoped rules remain references.

subagents.notes: Normalized access maps to native tool names and plan, auto-edit, or yolo approvalMode.

mcp.notes: First-party MCP entries and tools.approvalMode are deep-merged without replacing sibling settings.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skills use the same native roots.

kiro.summary: Kiro IDE 1.x and Kiro CLI package 2.x on its V3 agent engine ('CLI 3.0', selected with --v3 or --agent-engine v3), which share ~/.kiro and .kiro files: agent-surface generates one V3-format target for both. The CLI's V1 and V2 engines and Kiro Web and Mobile are not targeted. Kiro documents inconsistently whether Kiro CLI honors steering inclusion modes; not runtime-tested.

skills.notes: Canonical skills use current Agent Skills discovery and custom agents reference both user and project roots.

commands-as-workflows.notes: Manual-inclusion steering, invoked as #command-<name> or from / completion. Every generated agent lists all steering files as file:// resources, which Kiro loads when the agent starts, so those agents receive these files too. Kiro's steering page says Kiro CLI ignores inclusion modes and loads every steering file, while that page's capability table and the CLI 3.0 pages list inclusion front matter as supported: documented, conflicting, not runtime-tested. Manual inclusion is documented to hold where Kiro applies steering itself, as in the IDE.

rules.notes: Always and fileMatch inclusion modes preserve the source rule scope where Kiro applies steering itself and honors them, which is documented for the IDE; generated agents load every rule through file:// regardless, and for Kiro CLI the documentation conflicts (see commands-as-workflows).

subagents.notes: V3-format Markdown agents use tool tags, skill and steering resources, and capability permissions; their file:// steering glob loads every steering file at agent start, manual workflow files included (documented, not runtime-tested).

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services use native command-plus-args stdio entries.

settings.notes: User installs grant capability all with effect allow. Headless acceptance selects the V3 engine and trusts all tools (kiro-cli chat --v3 --no-interactive --trust-all-tools); immutable Kiro restrictions still apply.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skills use the same native roots.

notices.message: agent-surface writes its high-impact workflows as manual-inclusion steering files (.kiro/steering/command-*.md). Every generated Kiro agent lists all steering files as file:// resources, which Kiro loads when the agent starts, so those agents receive the workflows without #command-<name>. Kiro's documentation also disagrees on whether Kiro CLI honors inclusion modes: its steering page says the CLI loads every steering file, while its CLI 3.0 pages list inclusion front matter. Neither behavior is runtime-tested.
notices.action: Where a workflow must not load without explicit invocation, install Kiro without the asset categories that carry high-impact commands: --category development, and --category private when its local commands/ops-server.md overlay exists. To remove files an earlier install wrote, run the general Kiro install, which removes previously managed opt-in files, or delete the command-*.md steering files that the install root's .agent-surface/kiro-manifest.json lists.

antigravity.summary: The legacy Antigravity desktop target supports workflow files; current Antigravity CLI plugin packaging is generated by antigravity-cli.

commands-as-workflows.notes: Available high-impact commands remain manual legacy workflows; safe reusable procedures are native skills.

mcp.notes: Use the current antigravity-cli target for generated plugin packaging.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for Antigravity discovery. Available high-impact commands remain legacy manual workflows.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

notices.message: Antigravity retires its workflow format; Antigravity itself and its skills continue.
notices.action: Keep the generated workflow files; a replacement using native manual rules is not yet qualified. Do not convert them with /migrate-workflows, which turns manual commands into autonomously invoked skills.

antigravity-cli.summary: The Antigravity CLI target packages agent-surface as an agy plugin with skills, agents, always-on rules, scoped references, and external skills.

plugins.notes: Generated manifest packages the Antigravity CLI plugin.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are packaged in directory-form Agent Skills. Available high-impact commands are packaged as explicit-invocation compatibility skills with disable-model-invocation: true; host enforcement remains unproven.

subagents.notes: Normalized subagents are included inside the plugin package.

rules.notes: Always-on rules render as plugin rules; scoped language/security policies render as references selected by project-aware commands.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are generated into the plugin mcp_config.json (mcpServers); external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

external.notes: Registry-backed external Agent Skills are copied only from configured skill_roots that contain SKILL.md.

opencode.summary: OpenCode (npm opencode-ai), documented as a terminal interface, desktop app and IDE extension (the desktop app and extension are not runtime-tested here): agent-surface generates rules, commands, agents, canonical and external skills, first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire), full-access execution and disabled sharing in the default ~/.config/opencode or project roots. It does not write into OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR, an extra directory OpenCode loads after those roots and lets override them, and plugins are not generated. OpenCode 2 (npm @opencode/cli), which uses the same opencode command and roots, is not targeted or tested.

commands.notes: Available high-impact commands remain native custom commands; safe reusable procedures are native skills. Automatic sharing remains disabled.

subagents.notes: Subagents render as OpenCode agent markdown using current permission fields. Read-only roles deny all capabilities by default and allow only read/search/skill tools; writable shell workers allow the full tool surface.

rules.notes: Rules render as AGENTS.md.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for OpenCode skill-tool discovery. Available high-impact commands remain native custom commands.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are generated/merged under mcp; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in. Full installs apply the declared full-access/share-disabled host policy, while category-only MCP installs preserve existing host-wide policy.

plugins.notes: Plugin packaging is tracked separately from direct generated files.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

openhands.summary: OpenHands supports AgentSkills, AGENTS.md project instructions, plugins, hooks, and MCP; agent-surface generates AgentSkills, instructions, first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire), and registry-backed external skills while keeping plugins/hooks manual.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged. Available high-impact commands are emitted as explicit-invocation compatibility skills with disable-model-invocation: true; host enforcement remains unproven.

rules.notes: Project rules use root AGENTS.md. User-scope rules render as one legacy OpenHands skill because the verified SDK path loads user skills but not a user-global AGENTS.md.

mcp.notes: The verified OpenHands CLI reads mcpServers from ~/.openhands/mcp.json. First-party secretless MCP services are generated/merged there; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

external.notes: Registry-backed external Agent Skills are copied only from configured skill_roots that contain SKILL.md; the anthropic-cybersecurity source-pack remains served just-in-time by Grimoire.

plugins.notes: Plugin packaging can bundle skills, hooks, agents, commands, and .mcp.json, but is not needed for the minimal generated target. Hook and setup-script surfaces stay project-owned and are not generated by default.

notices.message: The OpenHands V1 CLI is no longer actively maintained. This retained adapter targets that CLI; it does not represent Agent Canvas or OpenHands SDK support.
notices.action: Existing CLI users can keep this target; evaluate a maintained OpenHands component separately before adopting it for new work.

vscode.summary: Default profile of stable VS Code, for the built-in Local agent harness: agent-surface generates profile instruction files, the profile mcp.json with first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire), and canonical and manual-only skills in ~/.agents/skills. Other profiles, Agent Host and cloud harnesses, Insiders and agent plugins are not targeted.

instructions.notes: Local agent only; relative to stable VS Code's default-profile Code/User directory. Agent Host sessions read their harness folders (~/.copilot/instructions, ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md, ~/.claude/rules) instead, and a co-installed copilot target can mask a missing file.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are generated into the VS Code user MCP config; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in. Agent Host receives forwarded VS Code MCP config except servers that need interactive input; unverified for these entries.

skills.notes: Canonical skills use VS Code Agent Skills discovery. Available high-impact commands install into the same root as explicit-only skills (disable-model-invocation: true). Current docs list ~/.agents/skills as a personal location without naming a harness and define disable-model-invocation: true as slash-only; live discovery is unverified. Prompt files were the legacy Local-agent route and are no longer generated.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

cursor.summary: Cursor desktop editor: agent-surface generates home-directory skills, commands, subagents and MDC rules (rule loading unverified), project .cursorignore files and first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire). Cursor CLI documents only project .cursor/rules and mcp.json, so for the CLI only MCP and, through --dest, project rules are documented; the home-directory surfaces are unverified there. Cloud Agents are not targeted.

rules.notes: MDC files under the home-only root. Cursor documents .cursor/rules as project rules and User Rules as a settings entry; loading from ~/.cursor/rules is undocumented and unverified. Existing files are retained.

commands.notes: Available high-impact commands remain native Cursor commands; safe reusable procedures are native skills. Current docs cover commands only through /migrate-to-skills, which converts user-level and workspace-level commands and keeps their explicit invocation; the former commands page redirects to Skills. Documented, not runtime-tested.

subagents.notes: Cursor readonly is binary; unsupported intermediate write-only tiers are refused.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are generated/merged; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for Cursor automatic skill discovery. Available high-impact commands remain native commands.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

droid.summary: Factory Droid supports .factory commands, droids, instructions, MCP, and skills; agent-surface generates the core .factory surfaces and optional external skill packs when submodules are present.

commands.notes: Available high-impact commands remain native commands; safe reusable procedures are native skills.

rules.notes: User installs use .factory/AGENTS.md; project installs use AGENTS.md.

subagents.notes: Normalized subagents render as Droid definitions.

mcp.notes: Optional MCP output is generated from registry/optional-services.json and non-destructively preserves any existing local MCP wiring.

external.notes: External packs are optional and render only when the corresponding submodule checkout exists and the service declares skill_roots.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for Droid automatic skill discovery. Available high-impact commands remain native commands.

copilot.summary: GitHub Copilot CLI (default ~/.copilot; COPILOT_HOME is not followed): agent-surface generates skills, custom agents, instructions and MCP at user and project scope; user installs also write one VS Code profile instruction file that only VS Code's Local agent reads.

instructions.notes: CLI-native instructions are generated at user/project scope; user installs also write a VS Code profile file that only VS Code's Local agent reads. The Copilot Agent Host reads ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md, which is not qualified here.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP servers use native command-plus-args entries. External or secret-bearing servers remain opt-in.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged. High-impact workflows remain explicit-invocation compatibility skills.

subagents.notes: Normalized access maps to Copilot tool aliases; headless full autonomy is supplied with --allow-all because Copilot has no equivalent persistent default setting.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same native skill roots.

trae.summary: Trae international IDE (TraeCode), which reads ~/.trae, the documented ~/.trae-cn/agents and the project .trae directory: agent-surface generates skills, explicit-only compatibility skills, the user_rules.md rules file, subagents and MCP. The CN IDE (trae-cn) and Trae CLI 2.0 (trae-cli) read other roots and are separate targets; ~/.trae/skills is co-owned with trae-cli and ~/.trae-cn/agents with trae-cn.

rules.notes: User installs write the single user_rules.md, which the locally installed 3.5.25 build loads beside the documented ~/.trae/user_rules/ folder (read from its app bundle); current documentation describes only the folder, and newer builds are unverified. Loading both would duplicate the rules. Projects get per-rule files every edition reads.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are merged into mcp.json beside the per-OS User settings (macOS Library/Application Support/Trae, Windows %APPDATA%\Trae), only once the IDE has created that User directory; the route comes from the locally installed 3.5.25 app bundle, not the documentation, and the Linux location is unverified. Project .trae/mcp.json is documented. Servers the pre-split target merged into a user ~/.trae/mcp.json, which neither the macOS nor the Windows build reads, are pruned. External or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

subagents.notes: The international subagents page documents ~/.trae-cn/agents, the same text as the CN page, so the route is co-owned with trae-cn; IDE discovery may need the Subagents directory beta toggle. Not runtime-tested.

skills.notes: Canonical and explicit-only compatibility skills; host enforcement of disable-model-invocation remains unproven.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same skill root.

trae-cn.summary: Trae CN IDE, which reads ~/.trae-cn and the project .trae directory: agent-surface generates skills, explicit-only compatibility skills, per-rule user rules, subagents and MCP. User paths follow the CN documentation and are not runtime-tested.

rules.notes: Per-rule files in the documented user_rules folder; projects share .trae/rules with the other Trae targets.

mcp.notes: The user mcp.json location beside the per-OS User settings comes from a third-party installer and is unverified; it is written only once the IDE has created that User directory. Project .trae/mcp.json is shared with trae. External or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

subagents.notes: Documented CN route, co-owned with trae; IDE discovery may need the Subagents directory beta toggle. Not runtime-tested.

skills.notes: Canonical and explicit-only compatibility skills. CN 3.3.63 makes both editions' global skill folders compatible, so installing trae and trae-cn together may list skills twice. Enforcement of disable-model-invocation remains unproven.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same skill root.

trae-cli.summary: Trae CLI 2.0 (traecli, TRAE Enterprise), which reads ~/.trae (TRAE_HOME is not followed) and the project .trae directory: agent-surface generates skills, explicit-only compatibility skills, subagents, project rules and the traecli.toml config with first-party MCP servers. Trae CLI 1.0 is not targeted. traecli 0.201.6 lists the generated MCP servers; the other surfaces are not runtime-tested.

rules.notes: The CLI reads AGENTS.md files and project rules and documents no user-level instruction folder, so user installs write no rules; where it reads a global AGENTS.md is unverified.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are merged into mcp_servers; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in. traecli 0.201.6 lists them as enabled (traecli mcp list, 2026-09-30).

settings.notes: The config merge sets approval_policy never and default_permissions :danger-full-access without replacing sibling settings.

subagents.notes: The paths come from the installed traecli 0.201.6 binary; project agents load only in trusted projects. Not runtime-tested.

skills.notes: The user root is $TRAE_HOME/skills at its default (from the installed traecli 0.201.6 binary), shared with trae; the project skills folder is unverified for the CLI.

external.notes: Reviewed external Agent Skill packs use the same skill root.

windsurf.summary: Windsurf supports workflows, rule files, skills, and MCP configuration; agent-surface generates workflows, rules, external skills, and first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire).

commands-as-workflows.notes: Available high-impact commands remain native workflows; safe reusable procedures are native skills.

rules.notes: Project rules use the Devin/Windsurf rules directory.

external.notes: External Agent Skills mirror into Windsurf skill roots.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are generated/merged; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in.

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged for automatic skill discovery. Available high-impact commands remain native workflows.

notices.message: Devin Desktop removed the Cascade harness in 3.9.19. This adapter targets legacy Cascade installs only; it is not Devin Local or CLI support.
notices.action: Use it only with an existing Cascade install; Devin Local and CLI need a separate target that agent-surface does not generate yet.

notices.message: Cascade documents a 6,000-character limit for the global rules file and 12,000 characters per workspace rule file. agent-surface's user-scope rules and any development rules exceed those limits today, and the installer does not block them yet.
notices.action: For complete rules in Cascade, use a project-scope general install, whose rules file fits one workspace file; user-scope or development rules may not load completely.

zed.summary: Zed supports AGENTS.md instructions, Agent Skills, external agents, and MCP context servers; agent-surface generates skills, instructions, external skill packs, and first-party MCP wiring (Synapse + Grimoire) in Zed's per-OS config directory: ~/.config/zed on macOS and Linux (XDG_CONFIG_HOME is not followed) and the roaming AppData directory on Windows (%APPDATA%\Zed by default), resolved from the profile home; a redirected %APPDATA% is not followed.

evidence.label: Zed settings file locations (docs source, pinned)

skills.notes: Canonical skills are emitted unchanged. Available high-impact commands are emitted as explicit-invocation compatibility skills with disable-model-invocation: true; host enforcement remains unproven.

rules.notes: Rules are bundled into AGENTS.md instruction files. The personal file is ~/.config/zed/AGENTS.md on macOS and Linux and %APPDATA%\Zed\AGENTS.md on Windows, which Zed documents as personal instructions for its native agent only. The Windows route is not natively qualified. A differing personal AGENTS.md that Windows installs made before the per-OS route left in ~/.config/zed is kept and listed as LEGACY_FILE_RETAINED, because Windows Zed never reads it; an identical one is removed after the replacement is written.

external.notes: External Agent Skills mirror into Zed-compatible skill roots only when the service declares skill_roots.

mcp.notes: First-party secretless MCP services are generated/merged under context_servers; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in. Windows installs made before the per-OS route merged into ~/.config/zed/settings.json, which Windows Zed never reads; the next full install prunes those entries there.

codex-plugin.summary: Export-only portable plugin package plus the local marketplace manifest a host's own plugin manager consumes. agent-surface renders the package; installation, caching, and removal stay with the native manager.

evidence.label: Plugin packaging and local marketplace testing

plugins.notes: One portable plugin manifest in the location the format specifies, plus the local marketplace manifest. The manifest declares the schema identifier the published manifest schema requires as a const; verified against codex-cli 0.153.2, where a manifest omitting it is rejected on install with `missing plugin.json` while the valid manifest installs, caches its companions, reaches model-visible discovery, and is removed cleanly. An earlier .codex-plugin overlay was compensating for that invalid manifest and has been removed. Paths are relative to the marketplace root passed to the host's `plugin marketplace add`.

skills.notes: Pilot scope is the single canonical ops-swarm skill and the companion files it already ships; the canonical source is rendered, not copied into a second maintained tree. Plugin-contributed skills are namespaced `<plugin>:<skill>` by the host, so the packaged copy does not collide with a direct-file install of the same skill.
